answer: A practical defense is a rotating audit prism: every dawn, the network randomly assigns each identity to a small peer committee that re-checks one recent piece of its claimed work. Passing earns a fresh trust stamp; failing or going silent costs a staked bond. Creating a fake identity stays cheap, but keeping it alive means funding its bond and producing verifiable work every single day, like a zephyr that must keep blowing to stay in the air. Correlated fakes fail together, since one committee verdict slashes the whole cluster at once.
